title: Delta Reign Pokémon: Release, Cards & Price Checks | CardScanFox
description: Explore Pokémon Delta Reign, released November 6, 2026. Learn what changed, how to identify your pulls and how to compare prices for the exact printing.
h1: Delta Reign Pokémon: What to Know Before You Check a Card Price
author: CardScanFox Editorial

sources.label: The Pokémon Company: Delta Reign release announcement

bodyHtml:
If you searched for delta reign pokemon, the expansion is officially named Pokémon TCG: Mega Evolution—Delta Reign. The Pokémon Company released it on November 6, 2026. This guide helps you identify the set, separate product formats and check a reference price for a specific card.

What is Delta Reign?

Delta Reign brings Mega Rayquaza ex back alongside Mega Golurk ex, Mega Malamar ex and Mega Golisopod ex. It also introduces Legendary Stadiums: two Stadium cards combine into one feature and form an extended illustration. According to the official release announcement, a booster that contains a Legendary Stadium includes both halves.

The expansion name identifies a group of cards. It does not identify one particular Rayquaza printing, rarity or finish. A search result showing a familiar character is only the start of a price check.

How to find the right Delta Reign card

  1. Read the name and full collector number on your physical card. Include any number after a slash.
  2. Check its language, expansion mark and finish. A foil treatment can belong to a separate price series.
  3. Search the Pokémon card database or card catalog. Match the artwork and details before selecting a result.
  4. Open the card detail and check its price source, condition and observation date.

A catalog search can return no matching record while a newly released printing is being added. That does not prove the card is fake or has no value. Use the official expansion information to establish its identity, then check catalog coverage again later. This page is a release and identification guide, not a complete official checklist.

Booster packs, boxes and individual cards are different products

Before comparing two listings, decide what you are buying. A sealed product price includes unopened packs and sometimes accessories. A single-card reference belongs to one identified printing. Do not divide a box price by the number of packs and treat that result as the value of an individual pull.

Likewise, a graded sale is not a raw-card comparison. Check the grading company and grade when the object is already encapsulated. CardScanFox's recent high-price ranking uses qualifying raw single-card references and excludes sealed products and graded prices.

How should you read an early price?

A published reference is an observation, not a guaranteed offer for your copy. Start with the price lookup, then confirm the dimensions attached to the amount. New supply, language, finish and physical condition can make two apparently similar cards poor comparisons.

A large percentage rise can start from a very small amount. On the seven-day gainers list, read both the starting and ending prices, plus their dates. The comparison follows the same price series exactly seven days apart. It does not describe every copy of the character.

Keep pulls and purchase plans separate

Once you identify a pull, record the copy you actually own separately from a card you hope to buy. Card AI provides Portfolio and Wishlist workflows for that distinction. Choose your download platform to continue in the app.

If you are also researching the anniversary products, read the 30th Anniversary UPC comparison. Delta Reign and 30th Celebration are different expansion names; using the correct name prevents a misleading price comparison.

title: Pokémon 30th Anniversary UPC: Day vs Night & Contents | CardScanFox
description: Compare the Pokémon 30th Anniversary UPC Day and Night versions, confirmed pack contents and promo themes. Separate sealed-box prices from individual card values.
h1: Pokémon 30th Anniversary UPC: Day and Night Compared
author: CardScanFox Editorial
bodyHtml:
The search pokemon upc 30th anniversary refers to the Pokémon TCG: 30th Celebration Ultra-Premium Collection. The official product showcase describes Day and Night versions, available in November 2026. This guide compares the confirmed contents and explains how to separate the sealed collection from the individual cards inside it.

Day vs Night: what changes?

Version Featured Pokémon ex pairing What to check before choosing
Day Pikachu ex and Espeon ex The version name and pictured promo cards
Night Pikachu ex and Umbreon ex The version name and pictured promo cards

Both versions belong to the 30th Celebration product family. The featured pairing is a useful way to distinguish the versions, but a familiar Pokémon name alone does not establish a promo card's exact identity. Read the collector number on each card before comparing prices.

Confirmed pack contents

Pokémon's product showcase lists 29 regular 30th Celebration booster packs and one Classic Collection booster pack containing three Classic Collection cards. It also describes accessories including a playmat, sleeves and a deck box. Check the official product page and the packaging for the version and region you are purchasing.

That pack breakdown matters: “30 packs” should not be read as 30 regular expansion packs. Nor does a pack count guarantee a particular card, pull rate or resale value. This guide does not assign a guaranteed value to the unopened contents.

Is the UPC price the same as its cards' value?

No. A sealed UPC listing describes the unopened product. A single-card reference describes an identified card, with its own language, finish, condition and observation date. Accessories and unopened packs are different objects again.

When comparing listings, make a short checklist:

  • Is the listing for a factory-sealed collection, an opened collection or just the empty packaging?
  • Is it the Day or Night version?
  • Are promo cards and accessories included, and does the listing describe their condition?
  • Does the price belong to your market and currency, and when was it observed?

CardScanFox's price lookup and high-price list focus on individual card references. They should not be used as a sealed UPC valuation or as proof that a box is a good purchase. This page does not provide live stock availability, a retailer offer or a sealed-product market price.

How to identify cards after opening

Use the full collector number and expansion information to search the Pokémon catalog. Keep regular expansion cards, Classic Collection cards and promotional printings distinct. If a record is missing, do not substitute a similarly named card from a different release.

The existing 30th Celebration card-list and price guide explains the anniversary catalog groups. Read it alongside the raw vs graded value guide when the prices you find appear inconsistent.

Record the cards you actually keep

An opened product can leave you with duplicates, cards to keep and cards on a future purchase list. Confirm each printing before adding a holding, and keep wanted cards in a separate Wishlist. Download Card AI to continue that collection workflow.

Looking for the other November expansion instead? Read the Delta Reign Pokémon guide before matching a card to the wrong set.
